description: Topi Rasku and the spine-tools project publish scripts that process heat-sector data for MOPO energy-system simulations. The native release is a computational notebook archive for deliverable D2.2. The related AmBIENCe workflow description locates this tool after European building heating and cooling calculations and states that it transforms those outputs into inputs for MOPO case studies. GitHub repository metadata identifies heat-sector data-processing scripts under the MIT licence. Zenodo provides the archived code freely; the separately catalogued raw inputs and generated time series keep their own licences and identities. Coverage is European heat-sector input preparation. Related records represent the upstream building workflow, source-input bundle and processed output collection. A limitation is that notebooks, file contents and execution were not inspected. Native metadata marks development inactive; GitHub is not archived. The repository description does not document every processing assumption, and the output dataset explicitly warns about approximate heat-pump coefficients and normalised demand.
